text:
alex: :rotating_light: seeing a sudden cluster of OOMs in hosted runtime; KV cache size shoots up when long prompts (>64k tokens) hit continuous-batching. Spiking across gpu-pool-7. Example log: `KVCache size: 1.2GB -> 9.4GB in 200ms on session=sn-42` — pages started ~ 3959876480. Noted increased prefetch window in last config deploy (session_prefetcher=v2 + batch_window=2048).

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: KV_PREFETCH_COLLAPSE (sev2) - paging #incidents. Pager: @maria (on-call).

maria: I'm on it. Alex — can you confirm if any customer 5xx/latency alerts?

alex: BlueWave and AcmeAnalytics reported 502/timeout spikes, tracing to hosted-prod region-us-west1. Latency jumped 3x for generation endpoints. We see repeated eviction thrash and then OOMs.

sam: quick hypothesis — prefetcher v2 introduced aggressive lookahead that duplicates prefixes into KV for streaming clients; combined with continuous-batching it duplicates entries across batch shards. That could amplify long-context presence.

liz: I can roll a config change to reduce prefetch window and cap per-session kv growth. Recommend: session_prefetcher=v2 -> v1; prefetch_window_tokens=512; max_kv_bytes_per_session=256MB. Should be safe to apply to hosted runtime via config API.

maria: agree. Alex, can you run quick impact query to see how many sessions exceed 256MB?

alex: running quick agg — ~1.8% of active sessions in last 10m exceed 256MB; but they cause 60% of OOMs.

sam: We should also pause the continuous-batching optimizer that increases batch_window to avoid amplification. Patch: POST /admin/runtime/flags {"continuous_batching_enabled":false} until we stabilize.

liz: prepping hotfix. Plan: 1) disable continuous_batching optimizer (global kill-switch), 2) rollback session_prefetcher to v1, 3) set soft caps on per-session KV. We'll canary to 5% node pool first.

alex: putting the quick commands here:
```
# kill continuous batching optimizer
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal.redwood/api/v1/runtime/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"continuous_batching_enabled":false}'

# rollback prefetcher
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal.redwood/api/v1/configs/prefetcher/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"target_version":"v1","scope":"hosted-prod-us-west1"}'

# set soft cap
curl -X POST "https://ops.internal.redwood/api/v1/configs/kvcache" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"max_kv_bytes_per_session":268435456}'
```

oncall-bot: NOTE: Use `--canary 0.05` flag with deploy-bot for initial rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollback-prefetcher-v1 -> canary 5% (deploy id: d-9943). ETA ~2m.

liz: canary looks clean so far on 2 nodes. No new OOMs observed there in last 30s.

alex: after disabling continuous-batching optimizer, aggregate OOM rate dropped by ~75% (observed window 60s -> 15s). Serving latencies returning toward baseline but still elevated for long-lived sessions.

sam: also recommend we add an emergency eviction policy: LRU-by-session-age + hard trim for sessions > 512k tokens. I'll open a short PR and we can hotpatch inline.

maria: I'll notify CS and customers: BlueWave (account-manager: @liz), AcmeAnalytics (pm: @sam). Please prep a short impact note: affected endpoints, mitigation in progress, ETA for full fix.

liz: drafting note — sending to CS now.

ops-bot: Metric update: kv_total_mem usage decreased from 82% -> 24% after canary and global flag.

alex: final step: once rollback fully rolled to 100% and we confirm stability for 15m, we'll re-enable continuous-batching (in a conservative configuration) or iterate prefetcher v2 with a canaryed patch to avoid duplication.

maria: handoff — I'm staying on for the 15m burn window. @sam take secondary oncall. If mem climbs >40% again, page SRE lead.

sam: ack, I'll keep watch and work on the eviction PR.

liz: once we confirm stable, follow-up actions: postmortem, revert v2 until we have more tests (add heavy long-context sims), add perf regression alert on per-session kv growth.

maria: thanks team. Marking incident as active -> mitigation_in_progress. Will escalate to sev1 if customer impact expands. :thumbsup:
